content.promptText:
<role>
You are a senior iOS/SwiftUI engineer and product designer who specializes in reverse-engineering best-in-class consumer dating-app interfaces into precise, production-ready design systems. You have shipped swipe-based dating products before and understand how photo-first UI, color discipline, and haptic-backed motion combine to make a matching flow feel alive rather than generic.
</role>

<reference_data>
Brand color system (one disciplined red, functional accents only):
- Match Red #E92434 (light) / Match Red Bright #F0203E (dark, Like button, active tab) — the ONLY brand hue
- Match Red Pressed #C81B2C; Match Ink #1A1A1A
- Light surfaces: Canvas White #FFFFFF, Surface Gray #F6F4F4, Divider #E7E2E2
- Dark surfaces: Dark Canvas #141414 (warm near-black, never pure black), Dark Surface 1 #1E1E1E, Dark Surface 2 #2A2424, Dark Divider #322C2C
- Functional accents (never decorative): Active-Now green #2ECC71, Super Like/verified blue #1FB6FF, Rewind/Premium gold #D6A75B (dark) / #C8923F (light), Boost purple #B36BD8 (dark) / #9B4FC0 (light)
- Text: Primary #1A1A1A light / #F2EDED dark; Secondary #6E6666 light / #A89E9E dark

Typography: Poppins (free substitute for the brand's Proxima/Poppins-family face) at weights 400/500/600/700/800. Wordmark is lowercase 'match' at 800 weight. Profile name sits at 26pt weight 700 with the age beside it at 22pt weight 500 — a deliberate weight drop, not a size drop. Interest chips are 12pt weight 600. Tab labels 10pt weight 600.

Named distinctive patterns to recreate:
1. Full-bleed profile card — the photo fills the entire safe area (behind status bar, above tab bar) with only a 20pt corner-radius inset, no card frame or margin
2. The action dock — five floating circles (Rewind 44pt gold, Pass 56pt gray X, Super Like 48pt blue star, Like 56pt solid red heart with no border, Boost 44pt purple) hovering over the photo with a deep 0 6px 16px rgba(0,0,0,0.5) shadow
3. Story-style segmented progress bars (3pt, white active / 35%-white inactive) across the top of the card, one per photo, with left/right tap zones to navigate
4. Frosted, translucent interest chips (white text on rgba(255,255,255,0.16), 1pt rgba(255,255,255,0.28) border, backdrop blur) laid over the bottom scrim — never solid-filled
5. The 'It's a Match!' full-screen celebration — a #2A1418→#1A1A1A maroon-to-ink gradient, two overlapping 56pt avatars with a 3pt ink ring, and a red-glow headline
6. The Likes You grid, where blur is literally the paywall: locked tiles at blur(7px) scale(1.2), one unlocked tile shown clear with a red heart badge
</reference_data>

<house_rules>
1. Never introduce a second brand color — Match is monogamous with its red; every other hue (green/blue/gold/purple) is reserved strictly for its one function (presence/Super Like/Premium/Boost) and must never appear decoratively.
2. Keep the profile photo genuinely full-bleed — no card margin, no drop-shadowed frame sitting inside the screen. The photo IS the screen; chrome floats on top of it, it doesn't contain it.
3. Preserve the name/age weight contrast (700 next to 500) exactly — this pairing is Match's signature typographic rhythm and collapsing both to the same weight loses the brand's voice.
4. Build the Like button as the single loudest object on any screen — largest size in its row, solid fill, no border — because Match's whole interaction model depends on one unmistakable primary action.
5. Use a warm near-black (#141414) for dark canvas, never pure black or a cool gray — Match's dark mode is deliberately warm to keep skin tones in photography looking natural.
6. Render on-photo text only over a gradient scrim, never directly on the image — legibility here is non-negotiable and is how the app avoids a text-on-photo contrast failure across arbitrary user images.
7. Keep interest chips translucent/frosted, never solid-filled — a solid chip would visually compete with the photo it sits on.
8. Animate the swipe with rotation tied to horizontal drag (not a straight linear slide) and commit with a damped spring — a card that doesn't rotate reads as static, not thrown.
9. Treat the 'It's a Match!' moment as the emotional peak of the whole app — full screen, not a toast — and never shrink it to a modal sheet or banner.
</house_rules>

<the_project>
- App name & purpose: [fill in — what does your app match or connect people around?]
- Screens needed: [e.g. Discover/swipe, Likes You, Messages, Profile, Match celebration]
- Clone vs. inspired-by: [literal Match clone for a prototype, OR adapt this red-monochrome + full-bleed-photo language to your own brand hue]
- Existing brand constraints: [any required brand color/logo/typeface that must be respected instead of Match Red/Poppins]
- Target iOS version & minimum device: [e.g. iOS 16+, iPhone SE up to Pro Max]
- Dark mode requirement: [required from day one / nice-to-have / not needed]
- Content model: [what does a 'profile card' represent in your app — a person, a listing, a place?]
- Any accessibility mandates: [e.g. must pass WCAG AA, VoiceOver-first user base]
</the_project>

<what_to_give_me>
1. A complete `Color` + `Font` + `LinearGradient` SwiftUI extension file with every token above, named consistently and grouped by role (brand / functional accent / surface / text)
2. A full component spec + SwiftUI code for the full-bleed profile card, including the story progress bars, bottom scrim, name/age/job/distance block, and frosted interest chip row
3. A full component spec + SwiftUI code for the five-button action dock, including per-button size, tint, and the press/scale/haptic behavior
4. A full component spec + SwiftUI code for the 'It's a Match!' celebration screen, including the gradient, avatar entrance spring, and CTA pair
5. A motion and haptics table — every named animation (swipe physics, like-tap pulse, match entrance, likes-grid unlock) with duration, easing/spring parameters, and which haptic generator call fires when
6. A dark-mode variant pass confirming every token's light/dark pair and where the warm-near-black rule applies
7. An accessibility pass — Dynamic Type scaling rules (what scales vs. what stays fixed), VoiceOver label phrasing for the profile card and dock, and color-contrast notes for on-photo text
</what_to_give_me>

content.promptText:
<role>
You are a senior iOS/SwiftUI engineer and product designer who specializes in reverse-engineering best-in-class consumer dating-app interfaces into precise, production-ready design systems. You have built compatibility-scoring and data-visualization UI before and understand how to make a numeric signal (like a match percentage) read as trustworthy and emotionally warm rather than clinical.
</role>

<reference_data>
Brand color system (magenta leads, indigo supports):
- OkCupid Magenta #E2024F: primary CTA, Like heart, active tab, match-percentage badge ring/number, selected toggles
- Magenta Pressed #C00244; Magenta Tint #FCE3EB (like-flash background)
- Brand Indigo #0500FF: Pass affordance, secondary links, illustration accents — always secondary to magenta, never equal weight
- Indigo Tint #E5E4FF (pass-flash background)
- Canvas White #FFFFFF, Surface Neutral #F2F2F2 (cards float on this), Divider #E5E5E5
- Match-percentage tiers: High (90–100%) #E2024F, Mid (70–89%) #F0578A, Low (<70%) #9B9B9B — gray de-emphasizes a poor match
- Text: Primary #14171A, Secondary #6B6B6B, Tertiary #9B9B9B
- Dark mode (limited/secondary theme): Canvas #15151A, Surface #1F1F26, magenta stays #E2024F unchanged

Typography: Larsseit (brand face; Inter is the closest free substitute) at weights 400/600/700 only — no thin weight anywhere. Screen titles 30pt weight 700 with -0.4pt tracking. Question prompts sit at a generous 20pt weight 600 — deliberately large because the compatibility questions are the core engagement loop, not an afterthought. The match-percentage number is set at 20pt weight 700 inside its badge.

Named distinctive patterns to recreate:
1. The circular match-percentage badge — a 48pt (card) / 36pt (list) ring whose stroke color is tiered by score, with the number counting up from 0 on first appearance over ~600ms
2. DoubleTake — a rich, internally-scrollable profile card (not a thin swipe deck) combining a hero photo, bio, and question-answer highlights before a decision is made
3. The match-question card — a rounded white card with a bold prompt, a stack of full-width answer-option pills, and an 'importance' segmented control beneath
4. Two-color (magenta + indigo) illustrated empty and success states — a deliberate warmth choice instead of a sterile blank screen
5. The Like/Pass button pairing — a 64pt magenta-heart circle vs. a 56pt indigo-X circle, sized asymmetrically so Like reads as the primary action
6. The 'It's a Match' full-screen celebration, magenta-led with both avatars and a joyful, non-sterile tone
</reference_data>

<house_rules>
1. Let magenta lead and indigo support on every screen — never give the two accent colors equal visual weight on the same control; magenta is always the dominant one.
2. Make the match-percentage badge loud when it's a great match — bold, large, magenta — and quietly gray when it's a poor one; never invert this (a small gray badge on a 95% match would contradict the whole point of the feature).
3. Never reduce a profile to a thin single-photo swipe card — DoubleTake is deliberately rich and scrollable, because OkCupid's positioning is 'substance over swipe.'
4. Round generously and consistently — 20–24pt on cards, full pill radius on every button and answer option — sharp corners read off-brand here.
5. Use only the three defined weights (400/600/700) throughout; introducing a thin weight undercuts the friendly-but-confident voice the type system is built around.
6. Always animate the match-percentage number counting up rather than appearing instantly — this small motion detail is what makes the data feel alive rather than static.
7. Never ship a sterile blank empty-state — always use the two-color illustration language, because warmth in empty/error states is treated as a brand pillar, not decoration.
8. Keep the question-answer loop visually distinct from ordinary content cards (rounded, padded, pill-stacked) since it's OkCupid's core differentiating mechanic and should never look like generic form UI.
9. Respect Dynamic Type on titles, questions, and body text, but pin the match-percentage badge number and tab labels at fixed sizes since they are ornaments that break layout if they reflow.
</house_rules>

<the_project>
- App name & purpose: [fill in — what compatibility signal or data point does your app surface, if any?]
- Screens needed: [e.g. Discover/DoubleTake, Questions, Matches, Messages, Profile]
- Clone vs. inspired-by: [literal OkCupid clone, OR adapt the magenta/indigo + match-percentage language to your own brand]
- Existing brand constraints: [any required brand color/typeface that must replace magenta/indigo/Larsseit]
- Target iOS version & minimum device: [e.g. iOS 16+, iPhone SE up to Pro Max]
- Dark mode requirement: [full parity / limited secondary theme like OkCupid's / none]
- Does your app have an analogous 'compatibility score' or numeric badge concept: [yes/no — describe]
- Any accessibility mandates: [e.g. must pass WCAG AA, VoiceOver-first user base]
</the_project>

<what_to_give_me>
1. A complete `Color` + `Font` SwiftUI extension file with every token above, grouped by role (brand / match-tier / surface / text) and both light and dark variants
2. A full component spec + SwiftUI code for the match-percentage badge, including the tiering logic and the count-up animation
3. A full component spec + SwiftUI code for the DoubleTake profile card, including the scrollable internal content and the pinned Like/Pass/Star action bar
4. A full component spec + SwiftUI code for the match-question card, including the answer-option pills and the importance segmented control
5. A motion table covering the badge count-up, like/pass flash-and-bounce, and 'It's a Match' entrance, each with duration and easing
6. Guidance (with a code sketch) for the two-color illustrated empty/success state pattern so it can be reused across screens
7. An accessibility pass — Dynamic Type rules, VoiceOver phrasing for the percentage badge and Like/Pass buttons, and contrast notes for the tiered ring colors
</what_to_give_me>

content.promptText:
<role>
You are a senior iOS/SwiftUI engineer and product designer who specializes in reverse-engineering best-in-class consumer dating-app interfaces into precise, production-ready design systems. You have shipped high-density browsing UIs (grids, feeds) before and understand how to keep a content-dense, photo-forward grid feeling friendly and fast rather than cluttered.
</role>

<reference_data>
Brand color system (blue is the only brand hue; every other color is rationed by meaning):
- POF Blue #0098DB → POF Blue Light #00A6E2 (135° gradient): logo, primary CTA, active tab, the circular Like button, the Meet Me 'yes' button
- POF Blue Pressed #0079B0
- Online/presence (teal) #00C9B7 — used aggressively for 'Online' pills and 'Active now' text, including a slow pulsing dot
- Unread/notification (pink) #FF4F8B — reserved strictly for the Messages tab badge and unread indicators
- Upgrade/premium (gold) #FFB23E — reserved strictly for upgrade/premium surfaces, never used for anything else
- Light surfaces: Canvas White #FFFFFF, Background Grey #F4F5F7, Divider #E4E6EA
- Dark surfaces: Dark Canvas #121417 (cool near-black, never pure black), Dark Surface 1 #1A1D21, Dark Surface 2 #23272C
- Text: Primary #16181C light / #EDEFF2 dark; Secondary #6B7079 / #9BA1AB; on-photo text is always pure white

Typography: Nunito Sans (free, rounded, heavy-weight-capable — chosen to match POF's approachable, unintimidating brand voice) at weights 400/600/700/800/900. Card names sit at 15pt weight 700; section titles run 22pt weight 800; the display size (900 weight) is reserved for onboarding/large titles. This is a notably heavier weight ramp than most dating apps use.

Named distinctive patterns to recreate:
1. The match grid — a 2-column LazyVGrid of 3:4 full-bleed photo cards (16pt corner radius) each carrying a bottom gradient scrim with name+age and a distance/last-active meta line, plus a small circular blue Like button bottom-right
2. Meet Me — a single large profile card with three round decision buttons (✕ No / ? Maybe / ♥ Yes), the Yes button solid POF Blue with a glow, swipeable left/right like a lightweight card game
3. The 'Online' presence pill — a teal dot plus label, shown as a dark translucent pill directly on a photo card, with the dot pulsing on a slow 2-second loop to signal liveness
4. Messages as a first-class destination — a prominent tab with a pink unread-count badge, reflecting that POF has historically allowed messaging before a mutual match
5. The upgrade surface — the one place gold is allowed to dominate, used for premium/upsell CTAs only
6. A 5-slot bottom tab bar (Matches / Meet Me / Search / Messages / Me) with heavy rounded 800-weight labels always visible
</reference_data>

<house_rules>
1. Treat POF Blue as the only brand color for logo, CTA, active tab, and Like — never recolor it per screen or introduce a second 'primary' hue.
2. Ration every other accent strictly by meaning: teal only for presence, pink only for unread/notification, gold only for upgrade/premium. Swapping any of these (e.g. using teal for a CTA) breaks the color-as-meaning system this app relies on.
3. Build the app grid-first, not deck-first — POF's core browsing model is 'see many people at once,' so a single-card full-screen swipe stack should never replace the 2-column grid as the primary Discover surface.
4. Keep all on-photo text white over a bottom gradient scrim (never colored text on a photo) — this is non-negotiable for legibility across arbitrary user images.
5. Round everything generously (16–20pt cards, pill buttons, circular actions) and use the heavy 800/900-weight type ramp for names and titles — POF's warmth comes from rounded shapes plus rounded, confident type working together.
6. Never bury messaging — the Messages tab and its pink unread badge must stay visually prominent, since POF treats conversation as a primary destination rather than a locked-behind-a-match afterthought.
7. Show presence aggressively: a pulsing teal dot plus 'Active now' text wherever the data is available — presence is core metadata here, not a nice-to-have.
8. Keep profile photography full-color and undimmed in both light and dark themes — only the surrounding chrome should dim in dark mode, never the content.
9. Use a cool near-black (#121417) for the dark canvas, never pure black or a warm charcoal, to match POF's specific cool-toned dark palette.
</house_rules>

<the_project>
- App name & purpose: [fill in — what is being browsed/matched in your app?]
- Screens needed: [e.g. Match grid, Meet Me, Search, Messages, Me/Profile]
- Clone vs. inspired-by: [literal POF clone, OR adapt the blue grid-first + presence-forward language to your own brand]
- Existing brand constraints: [any required brand color/typeface that must replace POF Blue/Nunito Sans]
- Target iOS version & minimum device: [e.g. iOS 16+, iPhone SE up to Pro Max]
- Dark mode requirement: [required from day one / nice-to-have / not needed]
- Presence/online-status data: [do you have real-time online status to power the teal pill, or should it be mocked?]
- Any accessibility mandates: [e.g. must pass WCAG AA, VoiceOver-first user base]
</the_project>

<what_to_give_me>
1. A complete `Color` + `Font` + `LinearGradient` SwiftUI extension file with every token above, grouped by role (brand / presence / unread / upgrade / surface / text)
2. A full component spec + SwiftUI code for the profile grid card and the LazyVGrid match-grid layout
3. A full component spec + SwiftUI code for the Meet Me card, including the three round decision buttons and the left/right swipe-to-decide gesture
4. A full component spec + SwiftUI code for the pulsing 'Online' presence pill and the pink unread-badge pattern used on the tab bar and conversation rows
5. A motion table covering the grid-card like pop, the Meet Me decision slide-off, the presence-dot pulse, and skeleton-loading shimmer, each with duration/easing
6. A dark-mode pass confirming the cool-near-black token mapping and which elements (chrome vs. photography) are allowed to dim

content.promptText:
<role>
You are a senior iOS/SwiftUI engineer and product designer who specializes in reverse-engineering best-in-class consumer dating-app interfaces into precise, production-ready design systems. You have built strictly monochrome, editorial-grade interfaces before and understand how to make restraint itself communicate exclusivity, rather than treating a lack of color as a lack of polish.
</role>

<reference_data>
Brand color system (functionally two colors, by design):
- Pure Black #000000 is the canvas — never warmed, never a charcoal substitute
- Pure White #FFFFFF is the ONLY accent — wordmark, the single primary button, the active story bar segment, the heart outline, primary text
- White Pressed #D8D8D8
- Surface 1 #0D0D0D, Surface 2 #161616 — barely-perceptible tonal lifts off pure black, never a colored surface
- Divider #242424, Hairline #2E2E2E — the only 'border'/depth cue in the entire system; there is no shadow anywhere
- Text: Primary #FFFFFF, Secondary #9A9A9A, Tertiary #5E5E5E; on-photo caption text is softened to rgba(255,255,255,0.92) rather than pure white, so it sits in the image instead of glaring
- Error #E5484D exists but is used only for destructive confirmations (leave/report) — the only non-monochrome pixel in the product, and rare
- Member media (the user's own photos/video) is the only intentional color anywhere

Typography: a clean, low-contrast neo-grotesque (Inter is the closest free substitute for the brand's custom face) at weights 400–600 only — there is no 800/900 heavy weight anywhere, mirroring the restraint in color. The wordmark is lowercase 'raya' at 600 weight. Profile names are 28pt weight 600. Role lines ('DIRECTOR · FILM & MUSIC') are 13pt, uppercase, letter-spaced +0.4px — the one recurring editorial-masthead tic in the whole type system.

Named distinctive patterns to recreate:
1. The full-bleed slideshow profile — a member is presented as an auto-advancing sequence of full-screen photos/video (not a static card), each timed like a social-media story
2. Segmented story bars (2.5pt, white when played/active, 30%-white when unplayed) at the top, filling linearly over each slide's duration, with left/right tap-thirds to scrub and a press-hold to pause
3. The music ticker — a small vinyl/note glyph plus '{Artist} — {Track}' text plus a 4-bar white equalizer that loops a height animation to imply live playback; the app is scored to the member's own chosen song
4. The editorial caption block — name, an UPPERCASE letter-spaced role line, a short bio, and a location, anchored low over a black-to-transparent scrim so the upper image stays clear
5. The white heart action — a 60pt circle with a 1px white border and an OUTLINE heart glyph that only briefly fills white on a like, never a permanent solid fill; white fill is rationed to exactly one button per screen
6. A hairline-only depth system — every seam between a surface and the canvas is drawn with a 1px #2E2E2E line and a barely-perceptible tonal lift, never a drop shadow
</reference_data>

<house_rules>
1. Never introduce a brand color of any kind — no like-red, no gold, no green success state. If a designer suggests adding color for 'affordance clarity,' the answer is a different white/gray value or an icon change, not a new hue.
2. Keep the canvas exactly #000000 — do not warm it to #0A0A0A or #121212 for 'friendliness'; the exact pure black is load-bearing to the gallery-frame effect.
3. Never render a drop shadow anywhere — depth is communicated only through a faint tonal lift (canvas vs. surface-1) plus a 1px hairline border at the seam.
4. Build the profile as a genuinely music-scored, auto-advancing slideshow, not a static card with a photo carousel bolted on — the pacing and the song are the product, not a decorative extra.
5. Set role lines in uppercase letter-spaced type without exception — this is the one recurring editorial signature in an otherwise minimal type system, and dropping it removes the 'curated creative directory' feel.
6. Keep the heart action an outline by default, filling briefly only on the like gesture itself — a permanently solid heart icon would ration white fill incorrectly and read as louder than the single primary CTA is meant to be.
7. Soften on-photo caption text to ~92% white opacity rather than pure white — this keeps captions feeling like they belong to the image rather than glaring on top of it.
8. Use exactly one type family for everything (no serif, no mono, no display face) — this mirrors the one-color rule and should not be broken even for a 'special' screen like onboarding.
9. Never tint, filter, or add a colored border to the member's own photography — it is the only color in the entire product and must render completely untouched.
</house_rules>

<the_project>
- App name & purpose: [fill in — what curated/exclusive experience does your app gate access to?]
- Screens needed: [e.g. Discover slideshow, Messages, Profile/settings]
- Clone vs. inspired-by: [literal Raya clone, OR adapt the monochrome slideshow language to your own exclusivity model]
- Existing brand constraints: [any required brand mark/typeface that must still respect the black/white-only rule]
- Target iOS version & minimum device: [e.g. iOS 16+, iPhone SE up to Pro Max]
- Dark mode requirement: [N/A — Raya is permanently dark; confirm your app should be too, or note if you need a light variant despite the source]
- Music/media integration: [do you have access to a real music-service API for the ticker, or should it be mocked?]
- Any accessibility mandates: [e.g. must pass WCAG AA, VoiceOver-first user base, reduced-motion support for the auto-advance]
</the_project>

<what_to_give_me>
1. A complete `Color` + `Font` SwiftUI extension file with every token above, enforcing the black/white/gray-only palette with no room for stray hues
2. A full component spec + SwiftUI code for the slideshow profile, including the segmented story bars, the music ticker with its looping equalizer, and the editorial caption block
3. A full component spec + SwiftUI code for the action row (Skip / outline Heart / Note), including the like-fill-then-fade interaction
4. A hairline-based depth system reference — every surface level (base/surface/sheet/modal) mapped to its exact tonal value and hairline treatment, with no shadow entries
5. A motion table covering slideshow auto-advance, story-bar scrub, the equalizer loop, and the caption entrance, each with duration and easing
6. Guidance for permanently forcing dark mode (`.environment(\.colorScheme, .dark)`) and why no light variant should be authored
7. An accessibility pass — Dynamic Type rules (what scales vs. stays fixed over media), VoiceOver phrasing for the slideshow and its scrub/pause actions, and a reduced-motion fallback for the auto-advance
</what_to_give_me>

<house_rules>
1. Ration gold to exactly its named roles (crest, hairlines, one CTA, credential marks, verification seal, active tab) — never let it bleed into body text or fill a card background by default.

5. Personify any human-curation feature in italic serif behind a gold left rule — this is what makes a recommendation feel like a concierge's voice rather than an algorithm's output.
6. Make scarcity visually explicit wherever the product is curated rather than infinite — a visible count, a 'next batch arrives at' message, generous surrounding black space — rather than implying abundance with an endless feed.
7. Keep the heart/like action an outline, never a solid fill, so gold-fill stays rationed to the single primary CTA per screen; a filled heart icon would break that ration and dilute the CTA's primacy.

<role>

You have implemented physics-driven drag gestures and card-stack UI before and understand how rotation, threshold-based commits, and haptic timing combine to make a swipe feel tactile rather than a plain drag-and-drop.
</role>

<reference_data>
Brand color system (a horizontal gradient identity plus a five-color action language):
- Brand Gradient: Tinder Pink #FD267A → Tinder Orange #FF6036 (horizontal) — reserved for exactly three places: the Match screen background, premium/subscribe CTAs, and the flame logo/active tab icon
- The five action verbs, each with its own dedicated color, never swapped or reused decoratively: Rewind gold #FFBD3B, Nope red #FF4458, Super Like blue #5D8DF1, Like green #00D68F (the LIKE stamp; the like/heart glyph itself renders in pink #FD267A), Boost purple #A952FF
- Canvas White #FFFFFF light / #121212 dark; Surface Muted #F5F5F5; Divider #E5E5E5
- Text Primary #424242 (a deliberately soft dark gray, never pure black) light / #FFFFFF dark; Text Secondary #737373
- Verified Blue #29B0FF; Match Glow Green #00D68F (also used for a pulsing new-match ring on the conversation list)

Typography: Tinder Sans (proprietary; SF Pro Display/Text is the practical substitute) at weights 400/500/700, plus an 800-weight italic reserved exclusively for the Match-screen hero moment ('It's a Match!' at 48pt). The card name/age formula is fixed: name at 28pt weight 700 followed by a comma and the age at 24pt weight 400 — never restyle this pairing. Swipe stamps ('LIKE'/'NOPE'/'SUPER LIKE') use the same 800-weight italic at 32–36pt, rotated 15°.

Named distinctive patterns to recreate:
1. The swipe card — a 3:4 portrait photo taking up most of the viewport, dragged 1:1 with the finger and rotated proportionally to horizontal displacement (roughly ±15°), committing off-screen past a distance threshold with a spring snap-back if released early
2. Rotated stamp overlays — 'LIKE' (green), 'NOPE' (red), 'SUPER LIKE' (blue), each in italic display type with a matching colored 4pt border, fading in as swipe distance crosses a threshold percentage
3. The five-button action row below the card — Rewind/Nope/Super Like/Like/Boost, each a white circle with a 2pt colored stroke ring matching its dedicated color, sized asymmetrically (Nope/Like largest, Super Like smallest/centered)
4. The photo paginator — thin white segmented bars at the top of the card, one per photo, with left/right tap-thirds to page through
5. The 'It's a Match!' full-screen takeover — the entire screen goes brand-gradient, with two circular avatars side by side and an italic 48pt headline
6. An icon-only bottom tab bar (Flame/Star/Chat/Profile, no text labels) with the active icon rendered in the brand gradient
</reference_data>

<house_rules>
1. Reserve the pink-to-orange brand gradient for exactly the Match screen and premium CTAs — never apply it to ordinary buttons or chrome, or the celebratory contrast of the Match moment is lost.
2. Never swap the five action-button colors — gold/red/blue/green/purple each map to one specific verb (Rewind/Nope/Super Like/Like/Boost) and that mapping is effectively the app's control-panel language; changing one breaks muscle memory for anyone who's used a similar app.
3. Keep the swipe card at a 3:4 portrait aspect ratio — this proportion is load-bearing to how the drag-and-rotate gesture feels; a squarer or taller card changes the physics feel even with identical code.
4. Always rotate the card proportionally to horizontal drag distance rather than sliding it in a straight line — a non-rotating swipe reads as a generic drag, not Tinder's signature gesture.
5. Render the LIKE/NOPE/SUPER LIKE stamps rotated ~15° with a colored border in italic display type — never present them upright or in the body font, since the rotation and italics are what make them feel like a stamped verdict rather than a label.
6. Use the softer #424242 for primary body text instead of pure black — this is a specific, deliberate brand choice, not an oversight.
7. Keep the tab bar icon-only with no text labels — adding labels changes the tab bar's visual weight and contradicts the spartan navigation model.
8. Trigger a haptic at the swipe-commit threshold and a stronger one on match/boost — motion without haptic feedback loses the 'slot machine' tactility the interaction is designed around.
9. Preserve the exact 'Name, age' formula (bold name, comma, lighter-weight age) rather than stacking them or using a slash/dash separator — this is a fixed brand typographic pattern.
</house_rules>

- Any accessibility mandates: [e.g. must pass WCAG AA, VoiceOver-first user base, Reduce Motion support]
</the_project>
